entry: City and municipality in central [[Spain]] and capital of Toledo province (pop., 2024: 86,526). Built on a Carpetanian settlement, it became a Roman city and later the capital of the [[Visigothic Kingdom]]. Under Islamic rule it was a center of exchange between the Islamic world and Latin Christendom, and Christian forces took it in 1085. After losing political power to [[Madrid]], its economy stayed afloat on the [[Silk|silk industry]] until it declined from the 1630s. The city is known for its Gothic cathedral and bladed weapons. [[UNESCO]] declared it a [[World Heritage Site]] in 1986.

Colorless, water-insoluble aromatic hydrocarbon, C₆H₅CH₃, also called toluol or methylbenzene. It has a sweet smell and contributes to the aroma of [[Gasoline|gasoline]] and paint fumes. It is mainly used as an industrial feedstock and solvent, including in some paint thinners and glues. Nitration of toluene yields explosives such as trinitrotoluene ([[TNT]]). It was first isolated in 1837 and named *toluène* by Auguste Cahours in 1850. Recreational inhalation can cause severe neurological harm.

American football quarterback. Brady played 23 seasons in the [[National Football League|National Football League (NFL)]], 20 of them with the [[New England Patriots]] and his last three with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Selected 199th overall in the sixth round of the 2000 NFL draft, he became the Patriots' starter in his second season and led them to their first [[Super Bowl|Super Bowl XXXVI]] title. As the team's primary starter for 18 seasons, he won six Super Bowl titles with New England and seven overall. He holds NFL records for career passing yards, completions and touchdown passes. He was the first unanimous NFL Most Valuable Player and has the most Pro Bowl selections. In 2024 he became lead color commentator for NFL games on Fox.

American writer of techno-thrillers that feature technical detail in [[Espionage|espionage]] and [[Military science|military science]] settings. Originally an [[Insurance|insurance agent]], he published his first novel, *The Hunt for Red October*, in 1984. Eighteen novels followed between 1986 and 2013. His Ryanverse series, featuring analyst Jack Ryan of the [[Central Intelligence Agency]], is among the best-selling fiction series, with more than 100 million copies in print. Clancy also wrote nonfiction on military subjects, and his creations inspired video games such as *Rainbow Six* and *Splinter Cell*.

American actor and film producer. Cruise broke through with *Risky Business* (1983) and *Top Gun* (1986). He won a Golden Globe Award and was nominated for an [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for *Born on the Fourth of July* (1989). He is known for performing his own stunts as Ethan Hunt in the *Mission: Impossible* series. His films have grossed over $13.3 billion worldwide. He is an outspoken advocate of the [[Scientology|Church of Scientology]], which has drawn controversy and scrutiny.

American fashion designer and filmmaker. Ford was creative director at Gucci and at [[Yves Saint Laurent (designer)|Yves Saint Laurent]] before launching his eponymous fashion brand in 2005. The [[Disco|disco-era]] glamour of Studio 54 in New York was a major influence on his designs. He wrote and directed the films *A Single Man* (2009) and *Nocturnal Animals* (2016). He chaired the Council of Fashion Designers of America from 2019 to 2022.

American actor and filmmaker known for both comedic and dramatic roles, and one of the most popular film stars worldwide. He won consecutive [[Academy Awards|Academy Awards]] for Best Actor, for *Philadelphia* (1993) and *Forrest Gump* (1994). Hanks rose to fame in comedies such as *Splash* (1984) and *Big* (1988) and later starred in dramas including *Apollo 13* (1995) and *Cast Away* (2000). He has collaborated with director [[Steven Spielberg]] on five films, including *Saving Private Ryan* (1998), and he has frequently worked with [[Ron Howard]], [[Nora Ephron]] and [[Robert Zemeckis]]. He voiced Sheriff Woody in the *Toy Story* franchise and has hosted [[Saturday Night Live]] ten times. In 2016 he received the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

English actor and rapper. Hardy made his film debut in *Black Hawk Down* (2001) after training at the Drama Centre [[London]]. He rose to international prominence with *Mad Max: Fury Road* (2015) and played both members of the [[Kray twins]] in *Legend*. He received an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor for *The Revenant*, also in 2015. He has frequently worked with [[Christopher Nolan]], appearing in *Inception* and *Dunkirk*, and he played Eddie Brock and Venom in Sony's Spider-Man films. He releases music as a [[Hip-hop|hip-hop]] artist under the alias Frankie Pulitzer.

Welsh singer with a "full-throated, robust baritone," in the words of AllMusic. His career began with a string of top 10 hits in the 1960s, and he has toured regularly, with [[Las Vegas]] appearances from 1967 to 2011. He has sold over 100 million records, with 36 Top 40 hits in the U.K. and 19 in the U.S. Hits include "It's Not Unusual" and "Delilah." He was knighted by [[Elizabeth II|Queen Elizabeth II]] in 2006 for services to music. He coached on the television talent show *The Voice UK*.

American actor and comedian. Since 1999 he has voiced the title character in [[SpongeBob SquarePants]] and its associated media. Kenny performed stand-up comedy for eight years before joining [[Nickelodeon]] in 1993 after being cast in *Rocko's Modern Life*. His other voice roles include the Ice King in *Adventure Time* and the Narrator and Mayor in *The Powerpuff Girls*. He has received two Daytime Emmy Awards and two Annie Awards for his voice work.

American [[Rock music|rock]] singer, songwriter and guitarist. He was the frontman of Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers and a member of the late 1980s supergroup the Traveling Wilburys. He sold more than 80 million records worldwide. Hits with the Heartbreakers include "American Girl" (1976) and "Refugee" (1980), and his solo hits include "I Won't Back Down" (1989). The Heartbreakers were inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2002. He died of an accidental prescription drug overdose one week after the end of the band's 40th Anniversary Tour.

American actor best known for playing private investigator Thomas Magnum in the television series *Magnum, P.I.* (1980–1988), for which he won an Emmy Award in 1984. From 2010 to 2024 he played New York City Police Commissioner Frank Reagan in *Blue Bloods*. He played architect Peter Mitchell in the films *Three Men and a Baby* (1987) and *Three Men and a Little Lady* (1990). He enlisted in the California Army National Guard during the [[Vietnam War]] and served as an [[Infantry|infantryman]] until 1973. He was a spokesman for the National Rifle Association of America.

British playwright and screenwriter, born in [[Czechoslovakia]]. He left as a Jewish child refugee fleeing Nazi occupation and settled in England in 1946. He became a journalist and drama critic before turning to playwriting in 1960. Critics compared him with [[William Shakespeare]] and [[George Bernard Shaw]]. His plays include *Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead* (1966), *Arcadia* (1993) and *Leopoldstadt* (2020). He won an Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay for *Shakespeare in Love*, and he was knighted in 1997.

American singer, songwriter and actor whose gravelly voice delivers lyrics about society's underbelly. He began in the 1970s folk scene, and his music later drew on [[Blues|blues]], [[Jazz|jazz]], opera and [[Vaudeville|vaudeville]]. His albums include *Closing Time* (1973) and *Swordfishtrombones* (1983). He won [[Grammy Awards]] for *Bone Machine* (1992) and *Mule Variations* (1999), and he was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2011. He collaborated with Crystal Gayle on the soundtrack for [[Francis Ford Coppola]]'s *One From the Heart* (1982).

American animated comedy franchise created by William Hanna and Joseph Barbera in 1940. Its 161 theatrical shorts were produced by [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]] and center on a cat named Tom and a [[House mouse|house mouse]] named Jerry. Hanna and Barbera's MGM shorts won seven [[Academy Awards]] for Best Animated Short Film. After MGM closed its cartoon studio in 1957, the series was revived with shorts made in [[Czechoslovakia]] from 1961 to 1962, and the series now totals 166 shorts. The franchise also includes television series, a 1992 feature film, *Tom and Jerry: The Movie*, and a 2021 live-action/animated hybrid film.

Spanish Dominican friar and the first Grand Inquisitor of the [[Spanish Inquisition]]. He led the inquisition created in 1478 to uphold Catholic orthodoxy in the union of [[Kingdom of Castile|Castile]] and Aragon. He was confessor to Queen [[Isabella I of Castile|Isabella I]] and also became confessor to King [[Ferdinand II of Aragon|Ferdinand]]. Torquemada regarded converts from Judaism as a threat to religious and social life, and he was a chief supporter of the Alhambra Decree, which expelled the Jews from Spain in 1492. The Inquisition used torture to extract confessions and burned those declared guilty at the stake, and Torquemada approved of these practices. His name has become synonymous with cruelty, religious intolerance and fanaticism. At a general assembly in [[Seville]], he promulgated 28 articles of faith to guide the inquisitors' investigations.

Edible [[Berry (botany)|berry]] of the plant *Solanum lycopersicum*, a member of the [[Solanaceae|nightshade family]] that also includes tobacco, potato and chili peppers. The tomato originated in western South America and may have been domesticated there, in Mexico or in Central America. By 500 BCE it was cultivated in southern Mexico, and the [[Aztecs]] raised several varieties. The Spanish introduced tomatoes to Eurasia in the [[Columbian exchange]] in the 16th century, where they were at first grown as ornamentals. Today the tomato is a staple of cuisines worldwide, used in [[Pasta|pasta]] and [[Pizza|pizza]] sauces, soups, salsas and [[Ketchup|ketchup]]. Modern cultivars, bred to ripen uniformly red, number in the thousands, though breeding has reduced their sweetness. Global production was approximately 182 million tons in 2022.

Action-adventure video game franchise, with films, [[Comics|comics]] and novels, centered on the British archaeologist Lara Croft. The first game, developed by British studio Core Design, appeared in 1996 for [[Sega Saturn]], [[PlayStation (console)|PlayStation]] and [[Personal computer|personal computers]]. After Core Design's six games, development moved in 2003 to American studio Crystal Dynamics, the series' main developer since. The series has sold over 100 million units worldwide. Live-action films starring [[Angelina Jolie]] appeared in 2001 and 2003, and a 2018 film starred [[Alicia Vikander]].

British far-right, anti-Islam activist. Born Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, he co-founded the English Defence League (EDL) in 2009 and led it until 2013. His convictions include assault, threats, harassment and fraud, and he has served five prison terms. His self-produced documentary-style videos, including those on the grooming gangs scandal, have been found in court to include defamatory false statements. He declared [[Bankruptcy|bankruptcy]] in March 2021, and in 2024 [[The Times]] reported that he owed in the region of £2 million to creditors.

Island kingdom in [[Polynesia]], in the southern [[Pacific Ocean]] (pop., 2026: 103,291). Its 171 islands, 45 of them inhabited, cover about 750 sq km. By 888 BC settlers were living at Nukuleka, the earliest known inhabited town, and they were linked to the [[Lapita culture]]. From the rule of the first Tongan king, ʻAhoʻeitu, Tonga became a regional thalassocracy under the [[Tuʻi Tonga Empire]], which controlled much of the Pacific. Tonga was a British protected state from 1900 to 1970, but it never relinquished its sovereignty. In 2010 it became a semi-constitutional monarchy after reforms allowed its first partial representative elections. Captain [[James Cook]] visited in 1773 and gave the islands the name "Friendly Islands." Tonga is a member of the [[Commonwealth of Nations]] and the [[United Nations]].

Muscular [[Organ (biology)|organ]] in the [[Mouth]] of a typical [[Tetrapod|tetrapod]]. The tongue manipulates food for chewing and swallowing and is the primary organ of [[Taste|taste]]. Its upper surface is covered by taste buds housed in papillae, and it is kept moist by saliva. A major function in humans is speech, and in other animals vocalization. The human tongue has an oral part at the front and a pharyngeal part at the back. It has four intrinsic muscles that alter its shape and four paired extrinsic [[Muscle|muscles]] that change its position. The average human tongue is about 10 cm long, and its average weight is 99 g in adult males and 79 g in adult females. The word derives from [[Old English]] *tunge*.

American novelist and editor. Born in [[Ohio|Lorain, Ohio]], she graduated from Howard University and earned a master's degree from [[Cornell University]]. Her first novel, *The Bluest Eye* (1970), was followed by *Sula* (1973) and *Song of Solomon* (1977), which won the National Book Critics Circle Award. *Beloved* (1987) won the Pulitzer Prize in 1988. She became the first Black female fiction editor at Random House in New York City, and she later taught at [[Princeton University]]. Her works address the harsh consequences of racism in the United States and the Black American experience. She received the [[Nobel Prize]] in Literature in 1993 and the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President [[Barack Obama]] in 2012.

Metric unit of mass equal to [[Kilogram|1,000 kilograms]], symbol t. Also called a metric ton in the United States, it is distinguished from the short ton and long ton. One tonne is about 2,204.6 [[Pound (mass)|pounds]], 1.102 short tons or 0.984 long tons. The exact corresponding SI unit is the megagram (Mg). The symbol t was adopted in 1879. One megatonne of [[TNT equivalent|TNT]] is equivalent to approximately 4.184 petajoules.

British Labour politician and prime minister of the U.K. (1997–2007). He led the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] from 1994 to 2007 and rebranded it as "New Labour." He led the party to three consecutive general election victories. His government introduced a minimum wage, devolution in Scotland and Wales, and the [[Good Friday Agreement]] in Northern Ireland. Blair supported the [[2003 invasion of Iraq]], which was controversial, and as casualties mounted he was accused of misleading Parliament. He resigned in 2007 and was succeeded by Gordon Brown. In 2016 he founded the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change.

American actor whose career spanned six decades and more than 100 films. Born Bernard Schwartz, he was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actor for *The Defiant Ones* (1958), opposite [[Sidney Poitier]]. He co-starred with [[Marilyn Monroe]] in the comedy *Some Like It Hot* (1959). His stardom declined after 1960, though he later starred in the TV series *The Persuaders!* (1971–1972). He served in the U.S. Navy during [[World War II]] and married six times.
